newsitem.title: JAPAN: Major Japanese chain store starts selling US rice.
newsitem.headline: Major Japanese chain store starts selling US rice.

text.p: FamilyMart Co Ltd, Japan's third-largest convenience chain store operator, said on Monday it has started selling U.S. rice at its nearly 4,500 outlets across the country.
The rice comes from Arkansas, a major rice-growing region in the United States, and sells for 2,090 yen ($16) per five-kg (11-pound) bag, the firm said.

While it is a major international rice producer, the United States has had a difficult time selling rice in Japan, partly because most American rice is long grain and doesn't stick together well, making it unsuitable for such standard Japanese fare as sushi.
"The U.S. rice we introduced is as sticky as Japanese rice, and is nearly 40 percent cheaper," FamilyMart spokeswoman Maki Kimura said.

Under a General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade pact signed in 1993, Japan agreed to open its long-closed rice market and to gradually increase an annual import quota, but some consumers have complaining about limited access to foreign rice in local supermarkets.
The U.S. Rice Federation's Tokyo office said in a statement on Monday that FamilyMart's decision was a major breakthrough, given the number of outlets the chain has.
"I have no prejudice against foreign rice and would like to try U.S. rice if it's cheap," said Kaoru Satake, a housewife who was shopping in a FamilyMart store in Tokyo. ($1=124 yen)
